t: You're looking at St Paul's Cathedral, its high dome rising on Ludgate Hill, the highest point of the City of London. Christopher Wren designed this Baroque building, finished in 1710 after the Great Fire destroyed the earlier Gothic cathedral. The dedication to Paul the Apostle goes back to the first church on this site, founded in AD 604. Admiral Nelson and the Duke of Wellington are buried here. So are Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin, and the painter J. M. W. Turner. The poet John Donne was Dean of St Paul's from 1621 to 1631.
